meta.title: Onmal — your teammates' words, in your language
meta.desc: Understands your teammates' foreign language during games and shows it as subtitles over your screen, in your language. A free real-time interpreter that runs on your own PC.
hero.lede: Missing calls because you can't tell what a foreign teammate just said. Onmal listens for you and puts translated subtitles right over your game.
hero.note: No microphone involved. Your teammates' voices are processed inside your PC, and conversations are never sent anywhere.
how.h2: Subtitles appear before the sentence even ends.
how.lede: Four stages run back-to-back inside your PC. No server round-trips means no extra delay — and it keeps working if your internet drops.
how.t1: Only the app your team talks through
how.p1: In-game voice chat or Discord — Windows per-process capture takes audio only from the app you choose. Other apps' sounds stay out.
how.p2: Voice detection cuts out only the parts where someone is talking. Gunfire and music are filtered out; when it's quiet, nothing happens.
how.t3: Detects the language on its own
how.p3: No need to pick a language in advance. Russian or Portuguese — it detects and transcribes.
how.t4: In your language, over the game
how.p4: Click-through subtitles in a spot that doesn't cover the action. Your controls are never blocked.
name.p1: Onmal (온말) is pure Korean: on means whole or all — as in the whole world, all day long — and mal means words. Carrying a teammate's words across whole, whatever the language: that is what the app tries to do, and the name is that promise.
care.h2: Turn it on once, and it just works.
care.p1: Pick the app to listen to and your language — that's it. After that, just launch your game.
care.t2: Bring your own API key if you want
care.p2: The built-in translation is free. If you want higher quality, you can plug in your own API key. Keys are stored encrypted on this computer only.
care.p3: Audio is processed in memory and discarded. By default there is no recording, no uploading, and no account.
limits.h2: We also list what it can't do.
limits.lede: Better to know now than after installing.
limits.p1: Run the game in borderless or windowed mode for subtitles to appear on top. Most games have this in their display settings.
limits.p2: Capturing only one chosen app's audio works on Windows 11 (or Windows 10 build 20348+). Below that, all system audio is captured.
limits.p3: Even humans can't make out speech buried in gunfire and shouting. Neither can Onmal. When it fails, it says so instead of guessing.
limits.p4: No code is injected into game processes — nothing an anti-cheat would object to. The window-mode requirement above is the trade-off.
spec.h2:
It has to run alongside your game,
so we wrote these honestly.
spec.cpu_min: 4 cores · AVX2 (Intel 6th gen / Ryzen 1000 or newer)
spec.gfx_min: Optional — runs in CPU mode (subtitles arrive a bit later)
spec.gfx_rec: Vulkan 1.2 GPU — GeForce GTX 1650+, Radeon RX 6600+, Intel Arc A580+, with ~1 GB of VRAM to spare while gaming
spec.delay_rec: Under about 1 s (0.7 s measured on GPU)
spec.note: Delays were measured on an NVIDIA RTX 4060. AMD and Intel GPUs use the same Vulkan path but haven't been measured yet — that's planned for the alpha and beta stages. Accuracy is picked automatically to match your GPU memory, and you can change it in Settings at any time.
lang.h2:
Every language Steam supports,
for everyone on Steam.
lang.lede: The app and this homepage come in all 31 Steam-supported languages. Speech recognition covers far more.
road.h2: From 0.1 to 1.0 — completion criteria, not dates.
road.lede: Each stage moves on only when its exit criteria are met, not when a calendar says so. No rushing — and the base app stays free the whole way.
road.vision: The end picture is a companion you leave on whenever you game, as naturally as a voice chat app. Install it, forget it — the moment a foreign call comes in, Onmal quietly goes to work.
road.r1: The skeleton of real-time translated subtitles — local recognition, translation, overlay
road.r2: Stabilization — long sessions, running alongside real games
road.r3: Alpha test — a few testers go from install to subtitles with no instructions
road.r4: More translation — major language pairs bundled, OBS compatibility check
road.r6: Beta — Steam Playtest, speaker labels, per-game profiles
road.r7: Performance — low-end PCs and integrated graphics
road.r8: Release prep — store page, document review

road.r10: Full release — the always-on comfort of a voice app, still free
faq.h2: The questions we hear most before install.
faq.a1: Yes. The base app is free now and stays free after full release. No account, no payments, no ads.
faq.a2: Onmal injects no code into game processes — to the game, it is just a separate window floating over the screen. The final call belongs to each game publisher though, so check the rules first in sensitive settings like tournaments.
faq.q3: Which games does it work with?
faq.a3: It is not tied to any specific game. If the game can run in borderless windowed mode, subtitles can appear on top. For audio, pick whichever app your team voice comes from — in-game voice chat or Discord.
faq.q4: Do I need an internet connection?
faq.a4: Only once, to download the recognition model. After that, recognition and translation both run on your PC and keep working offline.
faq.q5: Does it translate my voice too?
faq.a5: No. Onmal does not use your microphone unless you pick it as a source yourself. It listens to your teammates' voices — the sound playing on your PC — and shows subtitles only on your screen. What you say goes out untouched.
faq.q6: Won't it slow down my game?
faq.a6: The game comes first — that is the design principle. It computes only while someone is speaking, picks the recognition model to fit your spare GPU memory, and ships with the heavy features off. Every PC differs though, so we will measure it alongside real games in alpha and beta and publish the numbers.
legal.h2: These documents are all that applies.
legal.lede: Onmal has no servers and no accounts, so the paperwork is short. The same documents are available inside the app. They are written in Korean, which is the authoritative text.
legal.p1: What is processed, and what is never collected. One-line summary: Onmal has no servers.
legal.p2: Conditions and restrictions — especially "only use it in conversations you are part of".
legal.p3: The open-source software, models, and fonts Onmal is built on, with their licenses.
